query: memory sizing indexes chunks steady state

text: Plan about 1,195 MiB (about 1.2 GiB) for the process, plus your application own memory. Per the Memory Sizing page: 300 x 500 = 150,000 loaded chunks; 150,000 x 7 KB = about 1,001 MiB. Largest index is 500 x 7 KB = about 3.3 MiB, twice that = about 7 MiB. Steady estimate = 186 MiB + 1,001 MiB + 7 MiB = about 1,194 MiB (186 + 1,001 = about 1,187 MiB just holding the indexes). This is above the 380 MiB model-load peak. If all 300 loads start together with the first one, they overlap the model load and can peak at about 380 + 1,001 = about 1,381 MiB; load one index first, then the rest concurrently, to stay at the steady estimate. Note: many small indexes cost 1.5 to 2x more per chunk than one large one, 7 KB is the upper-range measured figure (5.7 to 7.1 KB), and each extra process needs its own full copy.
